solidvue-solidvue-2026.tagline: South Korea's only LiDAR sensor IC fabless company

founders.background: Professor, Department of Semiconductor Systems Engineering, Sungkyunkwan University. Led development of Korea's first ToF image sensor and CMOS LiDAR sensor.
founders.notable_achievement: Published at IEEE ISSCC; CES 2025 Innovation Award winner

founders.background: Professor, Department of Semiconductor Systems Engineering, Sungkyunkwan University. Member of a joint research team with CEO Jaehyuk Choi.
founders.notable_achievement: Co-developed Korea's first CMOS LiDAR sensor

founders.background: Professor, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, UNIST. Alumnus of the same advisor's lab as CEO Jaehyuk Choi.
founders.notable_achievement: Participated in developing Korea's first ToF image sensor

solidvue-solidvue-2026.team_highlights: All three co-founders are top researchers in semiconductors and LiDAR. The R&D team is composed of veterans with over 10 years of LiDAR sensor experience. The company is expanding its design and mass-production organization.

product.summary: A fabless semiconductor company that designs and supplies CMOS-based, high-resolution LiDAR sensor systems-on-chip (SoCs).
product.problem_statement: Conventional mechanical LiDAR is bulky, expensive and vulnerable to vibration due to its motor and rotating parts, which limits its adoption in mass-market applications such as autonomous vehicles and robots.
product.solution: A solid-state LiDAR sensor IC that replaces all mechanical components with a single semiconductor chip. A CMOS SPAD array, TDC, image signal processor and power management circuitry are integrated on one chip.
key_features: 400×128 pixel high-resolution 3D point cloud output (based on SL-2.2)
Detection range up to 200m, 99.9% accuracy
Ultra-compact: sensor core 0.9cm×0.9cm, BGA package 1.4cm×1.4cm
Approx. 1/10 the volume and 1/100 the cost of mechanical LiDAR
Mass-producible on standard CMOS processes
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Single-chip CMOS SPAD (Single-Photon Avalanche Diode) sensor architecture. Built-in column-parallel multi-event TDC, on-chip histogramming and interference-rejection filters. Claimed to be the world's first single-chip SPAD sensor IC with 400×128 resolution.
product.target_customer: Automotive LiDAR module makers, robot manufacturers, drone and smart city infrastructure providers, and AR/VR device makers.
product.business_model: As a fabless semiconductor company, SolidVue focuses on designing sensor ICs, has chips manufactured through foundries (contract manufacturing), and sells them to LiDAR module and system customers. It currently supplies evaluation kits to global LiDAR module companies.

direct_competitors.name: Sony (Japan)
direct_competitors.comparison: Global leader mass-producing SPAD-based LiDAR sensor ICs, having taken the market early with its IMX series. SolidVue claims an advantage in resolution (400×128) and single-chip integration.

direct_competitors.name: Canon (Japan)
direct_competitors.comparison: Competitor in SPAD sensor development with strengths in long-range, high-sensitivity applications. Analysts view it as weaker than SolidVue in ultra-compact size and cost competitiveness.

direct_competitors.name: Infoworks (South Korea)
direct_competitors.comparison: Domestic startup developing FMCW-based LiDAR sensors. Because the technology differs, it is more a partner in market expansion than a direct competitor.

direct_competitors.name: Autoel (South Korea)
direct_competitors.comparison: Domestic startup developing LiDAR sensors for autonomous driving. The market is still in its early stages.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: South Korea's only LiDAR sensor IC fabless company. Achieves world-class 400×128 resolution in a single-chip SPAD sensor using CMOS mass-production processes. Approx. 1/10 the volume and 1/100 the cost of mechanical LiDAR.
competitive_landscape.moat: Single-chip SPAD integration technology and 14 related patents (as of 2023). Co-founders' track record of ISSCC publications and CES Innovation Awards. Monopoly position in the domestic LiDAR sensor IC market.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Globally, it is a late entrant behind Sony, but it differentiates on single-chip resolution, ultra-compact size and low cost. In the domestic market, it is the sole supplier of LiDAR sensor ICs and holds a monopoly position.

trending_reason.summary: A Series C round of KRW 16.3B, exceeding the target by 63%, raised in October 2026, makes SolidVue's IPO roadmap more concrete.

SAM consists of autonomous driving solution providers in Korea and Asia. SOM is still at an early stage.
market_outlook.market_trend: The shift from mechanical LiDAR to semiconductor-based solid-state LiDAR is accelerating. Competition in SPAD and ToF technologies is intensifying among global players such as Sony and Canon as well as startups. market_outlook.growth_potential: The CES Innovation Award and investment that exceeded its target are positive signs for securing global customers. Revenue is expected to surge once full-scale mass production begins in 2027. As the only LiDAR sensor IC supplier in Korea, it is expected to benefit.

enablefusion-2026.tagline: A 'fusion foundry' platform that designs, procures, and manufactures fusion equipment.

founders.background: World-renowned fusion expert. Former head of the KSTAR project at the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy (KFE), and former Deputy Director-General and COO of the ITER Organization. Later served as Second Vice Minister of the Ministry of Science and ICT (South Korea).
founders.notable_achievement: Led the development of KSTAR (Korea's superconducting fusion research device) and served as head of operations for the ITER Organization.

founders.background: IT and management expert. Former CEO of KT and President of POSCO DX (formerly POSCO ICT). Has experience listing a startup on the KOSDAQ.
founders.notable_achievement: Former CEO of KT and President of POSCO DX; took a startup public on the KOSDAQ.

product.summary: EnableFusion operates a 'fusion foundry' called the Fusion Engineering Platform (FEP) instead of developing its own fusion reactor. It digitally re-engineers the requirements of global fusion developers, connects them to South Korea's precision manufacturing network (roughly 250 partners), and handles design, procurement, manufacturing, quality control, and installation end to end.
product.problem_statement: Fusion reactor developers struggle to source critical equipment with extreme specifications—such as ultra-high vacuum vessels, high-temperature superconducting magnets, and tritium fuel systems—for which global supply chains are narrow. Korean manufacturers that participated in KSTAR and ITER are highly capable, but it is practically impossible for individual startups to access this network.
product.solution: FEP (Fusion Engineering Platform) is a two-sided platform connecting demand-side fusion developers with supply-side Korean precision manufacturers. EnableFusion re-engineers developers' requirements based on digital twins, manages manufacturing processes, and takes responsibility for final delivery and testing. It consists of three categories: ① fusion components and systems, ② high-temperature superconductors (HTS), and ③ fusion AI.
key_features: Digital redesign and re-engineering of fusion equipment requirements
Operates a network of around 250 precision manufacturing partners in South Korea
Digital twin- and AI-based cyber-physical simulation
Manufactures vacuum vessels that withstand ultra-high vacuum, cryogenic, and high-radiation environments
Capabilities in high-temperature superconducting (HTS) wire, cable, and magnet manufacturing
Development of tritium fuel-related technologies
One-stop service from procurement, manufacturing, quality control, installation, and after-sales support
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Introduces the 'fabless semiconductor' model to the fusion industry. It is the first to commercialize the 'fusion foundry' concept, separating design and manufacturing in fusion, analogous to TSMC and NVIDIA in semiconductors. Engineering automation using digital twins and AI is the core technological differentiator.
product.target_customer: Global fusion startups developing their own fusion reactors (potential customers include Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Helion Energy), government-led public–private partnership (PPP) projects (ITER, DTT), and fusion R&D departments of major energy companies.
product.business_model: Project-based order and supply contracts. Revenue comes from fees and margins on the design, manufacturing, and installation of fusion equipment commissioned by customers. In the long term, it can expand into FEP platform usage fees or licensing models.

direct_competitors.name: Kyoto Fusioneering (Japan)
direct_competitors.comparison: A University of Kyoto spinoff and 'fusion systems provider' that designs and supplies core fusion systems (gyrotrons, fuel cycles, blankets). Like EnableFusion, it does not build its own reactor and instead supplies components and systems, but it focuses on Japanese and European manufacturers and partners with Germany's Siemens Energy and Proxima Fusion. EnableFusion's differentiation is its use of the Korean manufacturing ecosystem.

direct_competitors.name: Next Step Fusion (Luxembourg/UK)
direct_competitors.comparison: European fusion supply chain specialist founded in 2023. Specializes in integrated modeling, plasma diagnostics, and control solutions. More software and diagnostics-oriented than EnableFusion and does not have Korean manufacturing infrastructure.

direct_competitors.name: Bilfinger (Germany)
direct_competitors.comparison: Large German engineering firm that supplies magnets, cryogenics, and remote handling systems to fusion projects such as ITER and W7-X. As a large corporation, it has advantages in scale and references, but it is not a fusion-specific 'foundry platform'.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: It packages Korea's world-class precision fusion manufacturing capabilities—ultra-high vacuum vessels, HTS magnets, and more—accumulated through KSTAR and ITER into a single platform (FEP). It is the first to apply the semiconductor foundry model to fusion, letting developers focus on design without manufacturing risk.
competitive_landscape.moat: ① Exclusive network of about 250 Korean precision manufacturers that participated in KSTAR and ITER, ② the technical credibility of CSO Gyung-Su Lee, former head of KSTAR and COO of ITER, ③ global procurement capability proven by the EUR 26M DTT order in Italy, ④ close ties to government-level fusion R&D infrastructure (KSTAR, the Korean ITER project).
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: While most of the roughly 45 global fusion startups (as of 2026) focus on reactor development, EnableFusion is uniquely differentiated by its 'fusion foundry' business model. Rather than direct competitors, most fusion developers are potential customers. In the mid-to-long term, competition could emerge if large EPC companies such as Bechtel or Siemens enter the fusion market.

KRW 45B) vacuum vessel order from Italy's DTT project just three months earlier, validating the 'fusion foundry' model in the market. The symbolism of being South Korea's first fusion startup and the country's first fusion technology export is also drawing attention.

market_outlook.market_trend: ① Surging AI data center electricity demand highlights the need for carbon-free, 24/7 baseload power; ② Big tech (Microsoft, Google, Amazon) is rushing to invest in fusion startups and sign power purchase agreements (PPAs); ③ Governments are expanding fusion regulation easing and commercialization support policies; ④ Advances in high-temperature superconductors (HTS) make compact fusion reactors increasingly viable.
market_outlook.growth_potential: As the fusion industry enters a full-scale hardware procurement phase with the goal of commercial power generation in the 2030s, the role of the 'fusion foundry' is expected to grow. enablefusion-2026.editor_pick_comment: The distinctive positioning of a 'fusion foundry' that doesn't build a reactor itself but connects Korean manufacturers' ultra-precision technology to global fusion developers is impressive.

lomby-2026.tagline: Autonomous last-mile robot delivery in collaboration with Suzuki

founders.background: Formerly of Itochu Corporation; founded Yper (OKIPPA), a startup solving delivery issues, in 2017; pivoted to LOMBY in 2022.
founders.notable_achievement: Leveraged OKIPPA development experience, which solved the redelivery problem, to pivot into last-mile robot delivery.

lomby-2026.team_highlights: Currently attracting investment and pursuing technical collaboration with Suzuki, Mercury Investment, and others. As an engineering-focused team, it is carrying out NEDO-supported projects.

product.summary: LOMBY is an autonomous delivery robot that travels on sidewalks and delivers goods from stores within a 2–3 km radius to customers at a top speed of 6 km/h. Safety is ensured through remote monitoring, and operation is possible even in bad weather.
product.problem_statement: Aging and labor shortages make it difficult to secure workers for last-mile delivery. In Japan, especially severe population decline has made the delivery labor shortage a social issue.
product.solution: LOMBY robots autonomously deliver from stores to customers in place of people. Operating multiple units under remote supervision provides labor efficiency.
key_features: Autonomous driving and remote monitoring system
Durability and mass-production readiness co-developed with Suzuki
Compatible with existing smartphone apps and web services
Stable operation even in bad weather (rain, nighttime)
Reduces delivery costs to half or less compared with manual work
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: AI-based autonomous driving, route planning and obstacle avoidance using 3D maps, and a remote monitoring operations system. Classified as a 'remote-controlled small vehicle' under the Road Traffic Act.
product.target_customer: Businesses needing last-mile delivery such as convenience stores, retailers, and restaurants, as well as logistics companies and e-commerce operators
product.business_model: Provides robot delivery services on a per-delivery fee or regular subscription basis (est.). Validating the revenue model through demonstration experiments with 7-Eleven.

direct_competitors.comparison: A global leader that has entered multiple countries, but is not specialized for the Japanese market.

direct_competitors.name: Coco (Japan)
direct_competitors.comparison: An autonomous delivery robot startup in Japan operating similar delivery robots; the Suzuki-specific partnership is LOMBY's unique strength.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Secures mass-production capability and stable parts supply through an exclusive partnership with Suzuki. Government support such as NEDO and advanced remote monitoring.
competitive_landscape.moat: Suzuki's manufacturing network, proprietary autonomous AI and remote monitoring software, and experience in complying with regulations for road driving.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Although the market is still early-stage, it is building competitiveness through tangible results from Suzuki collaboration, government support, and 7-Eleven demonstrations.

trending_reason.summary: In a Series A round that closed in August 2026, raised ¥387M led by Mercury Investment, with participation from Suzuki, Nabtesco, Canal Ventures, and others, accelerating the buildout of a robot mass-production system.
catalysts: Labor shortage in delivery due to intensifying aging
Expanding last-mile delivery demand from e-commerce growth
Japan government's regulatory easing for autonomous robot demonstrations

funding.total_raised_note: Cumulative funds raised including the Series A (all through third-party allotment capital increases)

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: Japan's indoor and outdoor delivery robot market is projected to grow at an average annual rate of over 20% through 2030. LOMBY specializes in convenience store and grocery delivery.
market_outlook.market_trend: Labor replacement demand is surging due to aging and population decline, regulatory easing is expanding areas where robots can drive, and e-commerce growth is increasing the burden on last-mile logistics.
market_outlook.growth_potential: Targets deploying several thousand units in Japan within five years, with high potential for widespread adoption through Suzuki's mass-production capabilities.
risks: Potential changes in road-driving regulations (backlash if safety accidents occur)
Competition with robots developed in-house by major logistics companies
Technical limitations (complex intersections, narrow alleys)
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Suzuki's mass-production capacity and parts stability, technology advancement with NEDO support, and accumulation of real usage data through 7-Eleven demonstrations.

lomby-2026.editor_pick_comment: The strategic alliance with Suzuki gives it an impressive edge in mass production, but it still needs to prove greater technical maturity and operational efficiency to stand out in the global autonomous delivery robot market.

ellethermo-2026.tagline: Next-generation power generation startup converting waste low-temperature heat into electricity

founders.background: Associate Professor at the Institute of Science Tokyo. Inventor of the semiconductor-enhanced thermocell (STC).
founders.notable_achievement: Developed the core STC technology at the Institute of Science Tokyo and founded the company in 2023.

ellethermo-2026.team_highlights: A small deep tech team of science and technology experts. Brought in Mr. Ikami as Co-CEO & CFO.

product.summary: A power generation system based on a 'semiconductor-enhanced thermocell (STC)' that directly converts low-temperature waste heat (30~60°C) into electricity. Unlike conventional thermoelectric elements, it does not require a temperature gradient or cooling source.
product.problem_statement: Worldwide, data centers and factories generate enormous amounts of low-temperature waste heat, but existing technologies make it difficult to recover power, so most is discarded. Particularly in data centers, where power consumption is surging due to AI expansion, the need to convert energy used for cooling back into electricity is growing.
product.solution: STC applies the principle of chemical solar cells (dye-sensitized), using 'thermal excitation of semiconductors' instead of 'optical excitation of dyes' to directly convert unused heat near room temperature into electricity. It generates power simply by contacting a heat source, and when there is no heat, it can be switched off and 'recharged'.
key_features: Can generate power at low temperatures of 30-60°C (conventional thermoelectric elements require several hundred °C)
No cooling source required, minimizes installation space
Can be integrated with data center immersion cooling systems
Endothermic effect during power generation reduces cooling load
Works regardless of location (indoor, outdoor, underground)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: STC (semiconductor-enhanced thermocell) introduces semiconductor nanoparticles into a dye-sensitized solar cell structure, generating power through thermal electron excitation. Targeting 50W-class thermopanels.
product.target_customer: Data center operators, factory/plant owners, geothermal power generation businesses (hot springs, mines), automotive/mobility companies, home appliance manufacturers
product.business_model: Sales of STC cells, modules, and thermopanels; licensing; joint development. Initially supplying PoCs to data centers and manufacturers, aiming for commercialization by 2028.

direct_competitors.name: Gentherm (US)
direct_competitors.comparison: Based on thermoelectric generators (TEG) but requires a high temperature gradient. Low performance in low-temperature range and cooling plates are essential.

direct_competitors.name: Thermogenesis (Japan spin-off, est.)
direct_competitors.comparison: Reportedly developing similar technology, but specific differences are unclear.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Capable of generating power from a single heat source without a temperature gradient; no cooling source required. Can generate power 24/7 even in places without sunlight.
competitive_landscape.moat: Core patents from the Institute of Science Tokyo, STC principle patent portfolio. Technology credibility secured through joint demonstrations with major companies including KDDI.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Globally, elleThermo is virtually the only company with STC technology that converts low-temperature waste heat into electricity without a gradient. Optimized to solve data center power shortages, giving it a differentiated advantage.

catalysts: Surge in data center power consumption due to AI and cloud expansion
Japanese government's 2050 carbon neutrality goal and policies to utilize waste heat energy
Joint demonstration results with major companies including KDDI (waste heat power generation from immersion cooling)
trending_reason.growth_metrics: As of August 2026, achieved milliwatt-level power generation from a single cell; targeting commercialization of 50W-class thermopanels by 2028. Pilot production line to be established by 2027.

galux-2026.tagline: A biotech that uses AI to design proteins not found in nature from scratch.

founders.background: Professor at Seoul National University Department of Chemistry. Entered SNU Chemistry in 1989 as the top female scorer in the national college entrance exam. PhD from the University of Chicago. Postdoctoral researcher at MIT and UCSF. Professor at SNU since 2004.
founders.notable_achievement: Maintained global TOP3 in CASP (Critical Assessment of Structure Prediction) for over 10 years since 2010. Served as a CASP judge in 2018 and 2020, witnessing the emergence of AlphaFold firsthand.

founders.background: B.S. in Chemistry from KAIST, Ph.D. from SNU Department of Chemistry. From Professor Chaok Seok's lab. Oversaw investment, management, and business development in the early startup phase. Appointed Co-CEO in July 2026.
founders.notable_achievement: Key figure who proposed the startup to Professor Chaok Seok. Led the transition to a co-CEO system in 2026 and is preparing for an IPO in 2027.

founders.background: From Professor Chaok Seok's lab at SNU Department of Chemistry. Co-founder. Oversees macromolecular new drug (antibody) design.
founders.notable_achievement: Led the development of de novo antibody design technology on the GaluxDesign platform.

founders.background: From Professor Chaok Seok's lab at SNU Department of Chemistry. Co-founder. Oversees small molecule new drug and AI model development.
founders.notable_achievement: Implemented a proprietary approach to teach AI the principles of physics and chemistry.

galux-2026.team_highlights: In addition to the four founding members, the company recruited Kim Sung-hyun as CFO in May 2026, strengthening financial strategy and capital market response. With approximately 60-100 employees, the company has internalized both dry lab (AI design) and wet lab (experimental validation). The R&D center is located in Magok, Seoul.

product.summary: GaluxDesign is a platform that combines AI with the first principles of physics and chemistry to design proteins not found in nature from scratch (de novo). It supports various therapeutic modalities including antibodies, VHH, miniproteins, and cytokines, and has demonstrated a 1.1Å level agreement with Cryo-EM experimental structures.
product.problem_statement: Traditional antibody drug development relies on animal immunization or large-scale library screening, taking over a year with extremely low success rates. Difficult targets such as GPCRs and ion channels are nearly inaccessible with conventional methods.
product.solution: AI learns the physical principles of protein folding and molecular interactions, and given only the target structure, generates optimal antibody sequences within days. Through a fast feedback loop of dry lab design → wet lab validation, it achieves a hit rate of over 30% with just 50 designs.
key_features: Modality-independent: can design all protein therapeutic formats including antibodies, VHH, miniproteins, and cytokines.
De novo antibody design: generates new antibodies specific to target epitopes without existing antibody data.
Multi-parameter optimization: simultaneously optimizes binding affinity, stability, immunogenicity, and developability.
Cryo-EM validation: achieves 1.1Å RMSD agreement between AI-designed and experimental structures.
Over 30% hit rate with only 50 minimal designs: industry-leading design efficiency.
Expanding to difficult targets such as GPCRs and ion channels.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Unlike data-driven prediction models such as AlphaFold, the key differentiator is that it trains AI to learn the physicochemical first principles of protein folding and molecular interactions, enabling the AI to understand 'why this sequence is the answer'. Built on the GALAXY modeling suite accumulated over 20 years.
product.target_customer: R&D departments of global and domestic pharmaceutical companies and biotechs. Companies developing antibody and protein therapeutics, especially those interested in high-difficulty targets such as multispecific antibodies, GPCRs, and ion channels.
product.business_model: Upfront fee + milestone + royalties through joint research and development agreements. Targeting technology export or clinical entry after preclinical development of its own pipeline (PD-1/IL-18v immuno-oncology drug, etc.).

direct_competitors.comparison: Designs de novo antibodies with its own JAM (Join Atomic Model) platform. Partners with AstraZeneca and BMS. In a comparative study, Galux secured verified binding antibodies for 8 out of 9 targets (JAM-2 achieved 5).

Founded by former OpenAI and Meta researchers, designs zero-shot antibodies with the Chai-2 model. Raised a $400M Series C in July 2026 (valuation $3.8B). In a comparative study, Galux succeeded in 8 out of 9 targets (Chai-2 succeeded in 4).
Founded by Flagship Pioneering, has raised over $420M. Based in Boston. Designs various protein therapeutics with AI. Started earlier than Galux and has a capital advantage.
First to demonstrate zero-shot antibody design with generative AI. Partnership with AstraZeneca valued at $800M+. Listed company. Galux is unlisted with a technology-focused approach.

Protein modeling capabilities validated in CASP and CAPRI competitions for over 20 years. Fully internalized dry and wet labs enable a fast design-verification cycle.
competitive_landscape.moat: 20 years of accumulated protein structure prediction and modeling know-how at SNU Department of Chemistry. TOP3 in CASP for 10 consecutive years, 1st place in CAPRI. The physics-based AI approach can generalize to new targets without large-scale data. The 1.1Å level agreement with experimental structures (Cryo-EM) is the highest level in the de novo design field.

machenta-2026.tagline: Physical AI that enables robots to learn a task from a single demonstration through simulation-based training.

founders.background: Professor of Robotics at Imperial College London. As founder of the Robot Learning Lab, he led one-shot robot learning research for six years.
founders.notable_achievement: Author of foundational papers on in-context learning-based robot learning, including Implicit Graph Alignment (CoRL 2023) and Instant Policy (ICLR 2025).

founders.role: Co-founder (presumed to have served as CTO)
founders.background: He was a top doctoral student at Imperial College London's Robot Learning Lab, where he researched under Professor Edward Johns.
founders.notable_achievement: First author of the Instant Policy (ICLR 2025) paper, which introduced in-context learning to robots.

machenta-2026.team_highlights: An 11-person team formed when nearly all researchers from Imperial College's Robot Learning Lab joined the startup. The team has opened a new office and lab in King's Cross, London.

product.summary: Machenta develops robot foundation models trained exclusively on simulation data. It delivers 'Instant Robot Learning,' where a robot can immediately perform a task after a human demonstrates it once.
product.problem_statement: Traditional robot automation requires expert engineers to program robots for each task or collect large-scale real-world data. This is time-consuming and costly, and must be repeated every time a new task is added—a core bottleneck preventing robot adoption in industrial settings. Major VLA (vision-language-action) competitors are pouring enormous resources into collecting hundreds of thousands of real-world demonstration data.
product.solution: Machenta trains its models entirely in simulation, without using a single pixel of real-world data. The core is a Vision-Demo-Action (VDA) model that describes tasks through demonstrations rather than language instructions. Trained with a meta-learning objective that learns 'how to learn new tasks' instead of memorizing specific tasks, the model can perform a new task from just a single demonstration in the real world.
key_features: Single model handles all tasks: the same pretrained model is used without per-task fine-tuning.
Cross-embodiment: the same model runs on six different robots (including a humanoid).
Camera-agnostic: works with various sensor configurations.
Supports four teaching methods: leader-follower, VR controller, kinesthetic teaching, and bare-hand demonstrations.
One-shot one-person factory: three robots with different grippers and cameras automate an assembly line in two minutes, each using a different teaching method.
Runs on all hardware, from industrial robots to low-cost hobby robots.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The entire model is trained on meta-learning data generated in simulation. By generating countless random combinations of objects, tasks, environments, and embodiments, it optimizes the ability to learn tasks itself—so at test time, the real world is just another adaptation target. The company says this approach avoids the sim-to-real gap problem. Related research includes Implicit Graph Alignment (CoRL 2023) and Instant Policy (ICLR 2025) from Imperial College's Robot Learning Lab.
product.target_customer: It targets small-batch, high-mix manufacturing lines in industrial settings, factories that need assembly, packing, and tidying tasks, and small and medium-sized manufacturers that want to use robots without expert programming. It is also designed to work on hobby robots for home users.
product.business_model: Undisclosed. It is estimated to monetize by licensing its robot foundation model software to robot manufacturers or system integrators.

direct_competitors.comparison: A US startup building general-purpose robot foundation models through large-scale real-world data collection. Machenta takes the opposite approach: learning 'how to learn' from simulation alone, without real-world data.
A competitor that is scaling real-world data collection and beginning to adopt in-context learning. Machenta argues that simulation-based meta-learning can dramatically reduce data pipeline costs.
A new company implementing in-context learning through scaled real-world data collection. Machenta sees simulation, not real-world data, as a faster path to diversity.
A competitor pursuing a generalization strategy centered on real-world data collection. Contrasts with Machenta's simulation strategy.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: 100% simulation-based training with zero real-world data. While competitors pour massive capital into physical data collection, Machenta runs a meta-learning data flywheel in simulation, handling all robots, all tasks, and all teaching methods with a single model.
competitive_landscape.moat: VDA architecture built on six years of Imperial College research, plus a simulation data generation recipe. The core that is hard for competitors to replicate is the 'simulation data generation method that yields a meta-learning objective'—know-how accumulated by the company over many years.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: It proved its presence by raising $40 million at seed stage—the largest seed round in UK robotics history. Its scale falls far short of Physical Intelligence ($400M raised), but it is a lean 11-person team with a distinct edge, entering the competition with no real-world data collection infrastructure.

trending_reason.summary: The announcement on October 27, 2026, of a $40 million seed investment drew major attention as the largest seed round in UK robotics startup history. As the robot foundation model field races toward real-world data competition, the opposite approach—simulation-based learning—is gaining attention as an alternative.

Business Insider covers it in an article titled 'This 11-Person Startup Raised $40 Million to Train Robots...'
It is emerging as an industry alternative as the first commercial robot foundation model attempt trained only on simulation, in contrast to competitors that rely on real-world data.

The company is currently based at Naver D2SF @Gangnam and is expanding its research and engineering staff.

product.summary: Built on Phase-TITAN, a post-Transformer architecture that keeps memory usage constant regardless of context length, the company is developing AI agent and world model technology that runs on edge devices such as smartphones, vehicles, and robots without cloud calls.
product.problem_statement: In Transformer-based LLMs, the KV cache grows as input context gets longer, increasing memory usage. In on-device environments with tight memory, battery, and thermal constraints, it is difficult to run AI agents that understand long contexts and perform multi-step reasoning and tool calls.
product.solution: Phase-TITAN compresses context into a fixed-size 'evolving state' instead of a KV cache. This keeps memory usage constant even as the processed information grows, and enables the device itself to handle the full loop of calling external tools, interpreting results, and deciding the next action.
key_features: Phase-TITAN: a post-Transformer inference architecture that replaces the Transformer structure itself
PT Language Model v5: an on-device language model that supports long contexts and tool use without a KV cache that grows with tokens
PT Training-Free Dynamics Monitor: equipment condition monitoring that estimates normal dynamics for each device in real time without training weights
PT World Model: the first demonstrated persistent interactive video world model (33 minutes, real-time control across 10+ labs)
Runs multi-step agents on a single smartphone CPU core with fixed memory under 1GB (company demonstration)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Designed on computational neuroscience and physics foundations. Learns the world as a stable dynamical attractor using a fixed-size, attention-free temporal state. Does not use open-source models such as Qwen or Llama; develops its own models and keeps pretraining through inference engine in-house. At 1M-token context, the KV cache of a 1B-parameter model is 0.04GB (company measurement; a reduction of tens of GB versus comparison models).
product.target_customer: OEMs and platform companies for physical and digital edge devices, including automotive (global automakers, autonomous driving affiliates, and automotive software companies), robots, drones, smart glasses, wearables, and smart TVs.

oqt-2026.tagline: A KAIST spinoff developing error-tolerant quantum computers based on neutral-atom qubits

founders.role: CEO; also a professor in the Department of Physics at KAIST
founders.background: Born in 1985. Earned a Ph.D. in mechanical engineering at MIT with research in atom- and optics-based quantum technology, then served as a founding member of QuEra, a U.S. full-stack quantum computing company. Currently a professor in the Department of Physics at KAIST, and founded OQT in January 2025.
founders.notable_achievement: As a founding member of QuEra, which developed the world's first 256-qubit neutral-atom quantum computer, contributed to research results on logical qubits

oqt-2026.team_highlights: Reportedly co-founded by doctoral researchers from the KAIST Department of Physics lab. According to THE VC, there are two registered executive directors; total headcount is undisclosed. As of 2026, the company is continuously hiring in four areas: optical system engineering, system operations, quantum simulation, and quantum information (KAIST Munji Campus, Daejeon).

product.summary: A full-stack quantum computing company that designs everything from the quantum processing unit (QPU) hardware, which uses laser-cooled neutral atoms as qubits, to control software, error correction, and algorithms in an integrated manner. It aims to build error-tolerant, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on logical qubits, and as of October 2026 remains in the R&D stage prior to commercial product launch.
product.problem_statement: Quantum computers are vulnerable to external noise, causing errors to accumulate during computation. Adding more physical qubits does not solve the problem, as calculations still break down, so they cannot address real industrial problems. The key barrier to commercialization is implementing error tolerance that can detect and correct errors in real time.
product.solution: The company uses logical qubits, which bundle multiple physical qubits through error-correction codes, and builds error-tolerant systems through the Software-Defined Quantum Processor (SDQ), which reconfigures processor structure and operation to meet algorithmic requirements, along with co-design of hardware, software, error correction, and algorithms.
key_features: QPU that uses neutral atoms as qubits, cooled by lasers and arranged with optical tweezers
Logical qubit operations based on quantum error correction (QEC) codes
SDQ: reconfigures processor structure and operation in software according to the algorithm
Integrated co-design of hardware, software, error correction, and quantum algorithms
Large-scale scalability and power efficiency characteristic of the neutral-atom approach
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Neutral-atom arrays, Rydberg interactions, quantum error correction (QEC), and the SDQ architecture. The core driver is reproducing and advancing logical qubit technology, which the founder validated at MIT and QuEra, in Korea.
product.target_customer: Industrial companies and domestic and international research institutions working on drug and materials development and optimization problems. In the short term, the focus is on government quantum flagship programs and research collaborations; in the medium to long term, it targets proof-of-concept (PoC) projects with industry in Japan and the United States.
product.business_model: Undisclosed. As the company is still pre-commercialization, the leading candidates (est.) are QPU system supply and cloud access in a Quantum-as-a-Service model.

direct_competitors.comparison: A Boston-based U.S. company where OQT's founder previously worked. It has demonstrated the world's first 256-qubit neutral-atom QPU and the implementation of approximately 50 logical qubit operations, and is a global leader in neutral-atom technology with investment from Google and SoftBank.

A French company targeting 1,000-qubit-class systems using the neutral-atom approach. It is testing applications in finance and energy industries, including Crédit Agricole, and has partnerships with companies such as LG Electronics.
A U.S. company that uses strontium atoms and emphasizes long coherence times on the order of tens of seconds as its key strength.
A domestic quantum hardware company based in Daejeon that develops quantum measurement and control equipment rather than QPUs, creating an indirect competitive relationship.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: As a KAIST spinoff, it takes a co-design and SDQ approach that integrates hardware, software, and error correction from the outset. It is the only full-stack developer of neutral-atom QPUs in Korea.
competitive_landscape.moat: The founder's experience as a founding member of QuEra and in logical qubit research, a talent pipeline from KAIST labs, connections to the national quantum ecosystem such as the Korea Quantum Flagship, and the first-mover advantage of being the first domestic neutral-atom hardware company.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Effectively the leading domestic player in neutral-atom quantum computing hardware. On a global basis, it is a late entrant behind QuEra, Pasqal, and Atom Computing, pursuing catch-up through differentiation in logical qubits and SDQ. Through its 2026 pre-Series A, it secured a technology partnership with U.S. SRI and networks in Japan and the United States.

trending_reason.summary: Announced a KRW 14B pre-Series A funding round on October 15, 2026. DSC Investment led the round, with Kakao Ventures and Bluepoint Partners making follow-on investments, and Murex Partners, Stonebridge Ventures, Schmidt, ZVC, and GIL joining as new investors.
catalysts: KRW 14B pre-Series A funding on 2026-10-15 (led by DSC Investment)

Policy momentum, including the Korea Quantum Flagship (targeting a 1,000-qubit-class neutral-atom QPU by 2032) and Quantum Korea 2026 (July, DDP)

Valuation in the KRW 60B range was recognized during the pre-Series A process (based on Hankyung reporting, June 2026). Specific technical metrics such as revenue and qubit count are undisclosed.

unisieve-2026.tagline: A MOF molecular sieve membrane startup decarbonizing industrial separation processes.

founders.background: ETH Zurich alumni. Co-founded in 2018 after experience in strategic consulting and the energy sector.
founders.notable_achievement: Commercialized MOF membrane technology for industrial use and raised a $9M Series A in October 2026.

founders.background: ETH Zurich chemical engineering major.
founders.notable_achievement: Participated in the research of MOF-based membranes, the core technology of UniSieve, at ETH Zurich.

product.summary: UniSieve develops hybrid membranes that integrate MOFs (metal-organic frameworks) and zeolites into polymer membranes. They separate gases based solely on molecular size differences without heat, replacing energy-intensive processes like distillation.
product.problem_statement: In industrial processes such as petrochemicals, hydrogen purification, and carbon capture, separation and purification are mostly done via heat-based distillation. A significant portion of global industrial energy consumption goes to separation processes, a major source of carbon emissions and costs.
product.solution: Provides precise cutoff molecular sieve membranes that distinguish molecular size differences at the 0.1 angstrom level. Can save up to 90% energy compared to thermal separation and is supplied as container-type modules that can be fitted onto existing infrastructure.
key_features: Hybrid membrane integrating MOFs and zeolites into polymer membranes
Separates even similar molecules like propylene/propane based solely on molecular size differences
Up to 90% energy savings
Container-type modules that can be retrofitted onto existing facilities
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Based on MOF molecular sieve technology developed at ETH Zurich's Process Chemistry Laboratory since 2013. The core is the oriented arrangement of crystalline molecular sieves in polymer membranes to maintain selectivity at industrial scale.
product.target_customer: Energy-intensive industries such as petrochemicals (olefin production), carbon capture (cement, waste incineration, soda ash), hydrogen purification, and hydrogen blending in gas networks. Currently, chemical companies in Europe and the US are key customers.
product.business_model: Supplies container-type module systems directly rather than membrane components, scaling up from pilot tests to commercial use. Operated via software control and easily integrated into existing facilities.

direct_competitors.comparison: A Canadian carbon capture company based on solid sorbents. Uses MOF-based materials but requires heating and cooling cycles, not a membrane approach.
An early-stage startup for carbon capture from low-concentration flue gas. Raised €2.2M in 2025 and is not yet at commercial stage.
A US gas separation membrane company. Has commercialized CO2 capture membranes, but not MOF-based precise cutoff.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A hybrid membrane that separates based solely on molecular size differences without thermal cycles. Has prepared for commercialization simultaneously in olefin production and carbon capture, with the differentiator being the scaling up of MOF crystalline material into industrial membranes.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Among European carbon capture and industrial membrane startups, shows the most advanced commercialization results at the Series A stage. Has secured strategic investors like Orano Venture Fund and is conducting a real-world CO2 capture demonstration with Poland's Qemetica.
competitive_landscape.moat: Patents and manufacturing know-how for MOF-polymer mixed-matrix membranes, researched at ETH Zurich for over a decade. The technology, which aligns crystalline molecular sieves with uniform pore sizes within polymer membranes, is difficult for competitors to replicate.

trending_reason.summary: Raised a $9M Series A led by Orano Venture Fund on October 8, 2026, pushing forward the commercialization of MOF-based industrial membranes. The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry awarded for MOFs has also boosted interest in the material technology.

sonexos-2026.tagline: A Swiss deep tech startup using plasma to cancel low-frequency noise.

founders.background: Over 20 years of experience in active noise control. Founded SoundChip (now Synaptics) and sold it to the DSP Group. Bachelor's and Master's in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Auckland.
founders.notable_achievement: EY Technology Entrepreneur of the Year Award

founders.background: PhD from EPFL (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne). Originated the concept of plasma acoustic metamaterials. Published in Nature Communications. Worked at Schlumberger.
founders.notable_achievement: ABB Research Award, publication in a Nature journal

founders.background: Spent over 30 years at STMicroelectronics, serving as Vice President and General Manager of the MEMS division. Expert in audio semiconductors and sensors.
founders.notable_achievement: General Manager of the MEMS division at STMicroelectronics

sonexos-2026.team_highlights: CEO is the founder of SoundChip, which was sold to the DSP Group; CTO is an EPFL alumnus and developer of the core plasma acoustic technology; COO is a former head of the MEMS business division at STMicroelectronics with mass production experience.

product.summary: Sonexos has developed the 'Plasmacoustic Metalayer' technology that uses plasma discharge to actively absorb low-frequency noise. Unlike traditional passive sound absorbers, it is thin, lightweight, and has no moving parts.
product.problem_statement: Low-frequency noise (humming) from home appliances, HVAC systems, and data center cooling fans is difficult to control effectively with traditional sound absorbers or speaker-based active noise cancellation (ANC). As frequency decreases, absorbers become thicker, and headphone ANC performs poorly in 3D spaces.
product.solution: A layer of plasma (ionized gas) generated by corona discharge is actively controlled to absorb incident sound energy. The system detects the noise environment in real time and adjusts the plasma impedance, providing high absorption performance especially in the low-frequency range.
key_features: Thin panel format under 10mm thickness
No moving parts, lightweight, solid-state
Absorption performance up to 20 dB at low frequencies (below 100 Hz) for HVAC systems
Software-controlled adaptive active absorption
Sealed inert gas-filled package (Plasmapanel®)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Proprietary 'Plasmacoustic' technology using low-temperature atmospheric plasma discharge as an acoustic metamaterial. Based on core technology patented by EPFL, three generations of hardware evolution have reduced weight and volume by over 80%.
product.target_customer: Home appliance and HVAC OEMs, data center cooling system manufacturers, automotive parts suppliers, industrial fan/motor manufacturers
product.business_model: Supplies Plasmapanel modules to OEMs (B2B). Currently running paid integration programs based on engineering prototypes, with first mass production targeted for early 2028.

direct_competitors.name: Silentium (Israel)
direct_competitors.comparison: Provides ANC solutions for home appliances and IT, but is speaker-based with limitations in low-frequency spatial control.

direct_competitors.name: Soft dB (Canada)
direct_competitors.comparison: Provides active noise control for industrial use, but mainly limited to ducts or headsets.

direct_competitors.name: MuGen (Japan)
direct_competitors.comparison: Researching active absorption using magnetostrictive elements but is still at the pre-commercialization stage.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: The only approach using plasma as an acoustic absorber. Thin profile, excellent low-frequency performance, and does not obstruct airflow. Overcomes spatial limitations of speaker-based active control.
competitive_landscape.moat: Patented core plasma acoustic metamaterial technology, EPFL license, third-generation hardware and control algorithms, collaboration with global OEM network including Bosch Ventures.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Still at an early stage, but with clear technological differentiation and paid integration programs with major customers, positioning it to capture first-mover advantage.

founders.background: He is the co-founder and CEO of Vertical Insure, Slingshot's first customer and design partner. He has pointed out the gap between product design speed and carrier approval processes.

product.solution: Unifies insurance-related workflows into a single system and uses AI to automate data exchange and policy management between platforms and insurers. This aims to reduce the administration cost of micro-products and enable rapid product launch.
key_features: AI-powered workflow automation (policy management, data sharing)
API connections linking insurers, MGAs, and distribution platforms
Access to carrier relationships and capital connectivity for product launch and operations
Reporting and claims functions for micro-embedded products (specific features not confirmed in public materials)

product.target_customer: Vertical SaaS platforms, MGAs, insurance distributors. Publicly mentioned use cases include travel, amateur sports, and independent work (gig economy). The first customer is Vertical Insure.
product.business_model: Currently generates revenue as a technology provider working with external insurers. Ireland-based, data-driven distribution infrastructure that attaches insurance to vertical SaaS platforms via low-code widgets. It targets the same customer segment (vertical SaaS) as Slingshot.

Provides APIs for software companies to embed commercial insurance such as liability and workers' compensation. Competes in the commercial insurance space, with little overlap with Slingshot's micro consumer products.

helical-fusion-co-ltd-2026.tagline: Japanese developer of helical stellarator fusion power plants, based on technology from Japan's NIFS

founders.background: Began his career in Japanese finance, working at Mizuho Bank, JBIC (Japan Bank for International Cooperation), PwC Advisory and Dai-ichi Life. He then served as COO of a fintech startup before co-founding the company in 2021. According to his public profile, he holds a graduate degree in ethics from Kyoto University.
founders.notable_achievement: Founded the spinout based on NIFS research in 2021 and led it through a Series B 2nd close of ¥323M. He also serves as vice chair of J-Fusion, Japan's fusion industry association.

founders.background: A physicist with extensive plasma experiment experience. According to his profile, he has proposed several design concepts, including a fluid diverter, cartridge blanket, high-temperature superconducting magnets and functional liquid metals.
founders.notable_achievement: Has led the development of Helical Fusion's core plasma confinement and magnet design concepts. The official team page lists him as CTO, representing the company's technical direction.

founders.background: Described as having a graduate degree in nuclear engineering from the University of Tokyo. The official team page states he was a professor at NIFS and SOKENDAI, but the sentence structure does not make clear whether this refers to Dr. Goto, so this is treated as an estimate.
founders.notable_achievement: Introduced as Vice CTO on the official team page, and recognized for his expertise in fusion reactor design.

helical-fusion-co-ltd-2026.team_highlights: The team is centered on researchers from NIFS. The official team page also introduces a safety design specialist (from a national research institute) and business development personnel in finance and energy. The Fusion Energy Base profile lists Yosuke Kubo as COO. Speeda classifies the company as Series C, but the official announcement is a Series B 2nd close, so this article treats it as Series B. The team size has not been confirmed through public figures.

product.summary: The goal is to build commercial fusion power plants using the helical stellarator approach. Helix HARUKA, an integrated demonstration device, is currently under construction, and the first power plant, Helix KANATA, targets net electricity generation in the 2030s.
product.problem_statement: For fusion power to be commercialized, it must simultaneously meet three conditions: continuous operation, net electricity generation, and regular, efficient maintenance of components. The company argues that the helical stellarator can satisfy all three using existing technology.
product.solution: Based on research data from NIFS's LHD, the company is designing a device that combines high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets with liquid metal blanket and diverter systems. The structure is to validate the technology in a demonstration device before scaling up to power plants.
key_features: Helix HARUKA: An integrated demonstration device under construction at NIFS's Toki Campus (Gifu Prefecture). Energization tests planned for 2027
Helix KANATA: First commercial power plant targeted for the 2030s, with net electricity generation as the goal
High-temperature superconducting magnets: Demonstration targeted during the 2020s. Test coils reportedly passed performance tests under relevant magnetic field conditions
Liquid metal blanket and diverter: Performance testing targeted by the end of the 2020s
Helix Program official partner system: Launched in April 2026. Structure ties industrial suppliers and equity-investing companies to the actual construction of hardware
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The company chose a helical configuration built on roughly 70 years of accumulated Japanese stellarator research. The company explains that this configuration is well suited to continuous operation. Its core technologies are high-temperature superconducting magnets and liquid metal blanket/diverter systems. Helical Fusion has chosen the stellarator approach rather than the tokamak approach used by most fusion startups.
product.target_customer: Primary customers are power generation and electricity infrastructure operators and industrial partners. These include electric utilities, materials and component manufacturers, construction companies and energy firms. Recently, the company has also secured electricity demand-side customers, including a power purchase agreement (PPA) with regional retailer Aoki Super.
product.business_model: The model is currently based on joint development and corporate capital raising. Official partner companies participate in manufacturing and construction and invest in the project. After commercialization, electricity sales from power plants and equipment supply are expected to be revenue sources, but the specific revenue model has not been disclosed (est.).

direct_competitors.name: Type One Energy (US)
direct_competitors.comparison: Stellarator developer based in Knoxville, Tennessee. Announced a $200M Series B in October 2026, with cumulative funding above $400M. Plans to build the 400MWe-class Infinity Two at a TVA site and uses an integrator model that works with external suppliers. Far ahead of Helical Fusion in funding scale and utility partnerships.

direct_competitors.name: Proxima Fusion (Germany)
direct_competitors.comparison: Munich-based developer of quasi-isodynamic (QI) stellarators, spun out of the Max Planck Institute. Received additional investment after its 2025 Series A, and a valuation of $2.7B was reported for a July 2026 round. Targets an Alpha demonstration device in the early 2030s. The gap with Helical Fusion in valuation and funding scale is large.

direct_competitors.name: Thea Energy (US)
direct_competitors.comparison: Develops a stellarator that uses mass production of small pixel-shaped magnets. Completed a $100M Series B in May 2026. Belongs to the same stellarator family as Helical Fusion, but its magnet design philosophy differs.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A helical stellarator directly connected to NIFS, Japan's national fusion research institute. The structure also involves more than 30 large Japanese manufacturing and energy companies in development and manufacturing.
competitive_landscape.moat: Derives from national research infrastructure in Japan (NIFS LHD data, the Helix HARUKA site), an industrial partner network (Fuji Electric, Fujikura, Tokyo Gas, etc.), and supply relationships for high-temperature superconducting magnets. However, it has not been confirmed from public information whether this advantage is protected at the level of technology patents.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The company trails US and European competitors in the technology validation stage. Its strengths are industrial connectivity within Japan and participation in national projects. Funding and timelines for power plant construction are uncertain compared with competitors.

trending_reason.summary: On October 8, 2026, the company announced a Series B 2nd close of ¥323M (approx. $20.6M). Participating companies include Fuji Electric, Fujikura, Tokyo Gas and Hazama Ando. Attention increased as fundraising in the stellarator sector became more active during the same period.

market_outlook.market_trend: As fusion companies move into demonstration device and power plant construction stages, funding levels are moving beyond the venture stage. The stellarator segment has seen a continued series of large rounds from companies such as Type One, Proxima and Thea.

celaid-therapeutics-inc-2026.tagline: Developing cell therapies for pediatric hematologic diseases using cord blood hematopoietic stem cell ex vivo expansion technology

founders.background: He holds a Master of Engineering from Keio University and worked as a manufacturing and logistics consultant at Accenture. He later led the founding and management improvement of university-based biotech ventures, and oversaw business development and digital transformation (DX) for AI, IoT, and healthcare technology companies.
founders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Celaid in 2020 and has been CEO since; represented the company at the October 2026 Series B second closing announcement.

founders.role: Co-founder (Chairman of the Board and CSO at founding, resigned in December 2023)
founders.background: Graduated from the Faculty of Agriculture at the University of Tokyo, researched molecular immunology at Mitsubishi Yuka (now Mitsubishi Chemical), and gained research experience at the Ontario Cancer Institute and Mount Sinai Hospital in Canada. He served as CEO of CellFree Sciences and CTO of Megakaryon, among others.
founders.notable_achievement: Participated in developing Celaid's founding technology and led the company's early scientific strategy based on his experience in biotech technology management.

founders.background: MD, PhD, and is introduced as a specially appointed professor in stem cell therapy at the Institute of Medical Science, University of Tokyo. It has been reported that he also serves as a professor at Stanford University.
founders.notable_achievement: Along with Prof. Satoshi Yamasaki of the University of Tsukuba, they developed a technique for large-scale ex vivo expansion of mouse hematopoietic stem cells, which is the starting point of Celaid's platform.

founders.background: Introduced as a researcher affiliated with the University of Tsukuba and the Institute of Medical Science, University of Tokyo. Also written as Yamazaki in public materials.
founders.notable_achievement: Developed a method for ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells using polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) together with Prof. Nakauchi.

celaid-therapeutics-inc-2026.team_highlights: According to the official site, the founders are CEO Arakawa and Mr. Watanabe, while Professors Nakauchi and Yamasaki are introduced as origin of technology researchers. Employee count varies by source. Crunchbase says 1-10, parsed data says 11-50, Dealroom says less than 100, and one profile shows 201-500, which is low reliability. This report notes 11-50 but it is not a confirmed figure. Pitchbook and Tracxn list Masatoshi Sakurai as a co-founder, but this is not confirmed on the official site, so it was excluded. Yusuke Inoue is listed as COO and CFO on Pitchbook, but not cross-checked with the official site.

product.summary: CLD-001 is a cell therapy that uses frozen cord blood as raw material and increases the number of hematopoietic stem cells using its proprietary ex vivo expansion technology. It targets pediatric severe non-malignant hematologic diseases such as aplastic anemia, primary immunodeficiency, inborn errors of metabolism, and sickle cell disease. The company is preparing to initiate a Phase 1 clinical trial in the US.
product.problem_statement: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) is the only curative treatment for these diseases, but issues remain such as donor shortage, HLA mismatch, and graft-versus-host disease (GvHD). Cord blood can be used as a donor source, but the number of HSCs per unit is too low for adult patients.
product.solution: It uses units from frozen cord blood banks as raw material and expands the cell number with the company's ex vivo expansion technology. This allows selection of cord blood units with better HLA matching, according to the company.
key_features: Uses cells stored in frozen cord blood banks as starting material
Proprietary platform for selective ex vivo expansion of HSCs
Flexibility to select cord blood units based on HLA matching
CLD-001: Cell therapy for pediatric severe non-malignant hematologic diseases
Research collaboration and licensing of platform technology (joint research with AGC on expansion and functional evaluation of iPSC-derived HSCs, signed August 2025)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The original technology started from research on large-scale ex vivo expansion of mouse HSCs. Currently, adaptation to human cells, cell manufacturing process, and CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) development are underway. The specific compounds or compositions used for expansion are not disclosed in public materials. The company reported positive efficacy and safety data in animal models.
product.target_customer: Primary customers are pediatric patients with severe non-malignant hematologic diseases and transplant hospitals treating them. Secondary customers are pharmaceutical and biotech companies seeking cell and gene therapy research or HSC platform technology.
product.business_model: It pursues both advancing its own pipeline CLD-001 to clinical trials and offering the platform to pharma/biotech companies through research collaboration and licensing. Public materials mention multiple business areas: research support, media/reagent business, cell therapy development, and gene editing combination products. Revenue structure and contract terms are not disclosed (Undisclosed).

direct_competitors.name: Omisirge (cord blood HSC product, nicotinamide riboside-based)
direct_competitors.comparison: The goal of expanding HSCs from a single cord blood unit is the same. However, Omisirge uses nicotinamide riboside for expansion, while Celaid emphasizes the strategy of selecting units based on HLA matching. No data directly comparing clinical results of the two products was confirmed.

direct_competitors.name: Nicord (nicotinamide-based cord blood expansion product, Phase 1)
direct_competitors.comparison: It cultures CD133+ cells with nicotinamide for 21 days and then adds T cells. Phase 1 reported a median 72-fold expansion of CD34+ cells. Celaid uses a different expansion method and has no clinical data yet.

direct_competitors.name: UM171-related single cord blood expansion research (Phase 1-2)
direct_competitors.comparison: This approach uses a small-molecule HSC agonist. Safety and feasibility have been reported in clinical trials. Since Celaid has not disclosed the compound used in its expansion method, direct mechanism-level comparison is difficult. This class is a representative technical alternative that Celaid must contend with.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Based on public materials, Celaid's differentiators are three: first, using frozen cord blood banks as raw material; second, a design that combines expansion with optimal HLA unit selection; third, narrowing the indication to pediatric non-malignant diseases and progressing to US clinical preparation stage.
competitive_landscape.moat: Detailed patent list and scope are not disclosed (Undisclosed). Identifiable defensive elements: university-originated technology, in-house CMC process established, US CDMO technology transfer completed, FDA Pre-IND meeting completed, AMED grant selection.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: CLD-001 is still pre-Phase 1. Shionogi's entry as a new investor is a strategic signal. However, cumulative funding of approx. $22.1M is small compared to large competitors, and clinical data comparison with competing technologies has not been performed.

pit-in-2026.tagline: A distributed energy platform connecting commercial EV battery swapping and subscription stations to the power grid

founders.background: Worked as a researcher at Hyundai Motor Group for 15 years, participating in the development of the first-generation Kia K5, Hyundai Santa Fe DM, Genesis G80, etc. Founded PIT IN after noticing battery pack SOH (lifespan) issues and insufficient charging infrastructure for commercial EVs.
founders.notable_achievement: Credited with spinning off PIT IN, which started as an internal startup at Hyundai Motor Group, in just 9 months. It was introduced as the fastest early spin-off among Hyundai Motor Group's internal startups.

pit-in-2026.team_highlights: As of August 2026, the company had 21 employees according to The VC, but a recruitment platform lists 30, so the exact number is unconfirmed. We were unable to verify public profiles of key executives other than the CEO. With Hyundai Motor Group as a shareholder, the connection to automotive development talent appears to be a strength.

product.summary: It operates stations that provide battery swapping services, subscription-based battery management, and membership charging for commercial EVs (taxis, trucks, etc.). Currently, it is expanding beyond battery swapping stations into a 'distributed energy platform' that connects stations to the power grid.
product.problem_statement: Commercial EVs have long daily operating hours, so charging wait times lead to productivity losses, and battery SOH uncertainty adds to vehicle operating costs. Charging infrastructure is also insufficient for commercial vehicles.
product.solution: It reduces charging wait times by swapping batteries, and manages batteries through a subscription model to lower drivers' upfront costs and battery risks. At stations, it aims to reduce electricity costs through charge/discharge scheduling and peak power management.
key_features: Battery swapping service and subscription-based battery management
Membership charging and station ancillary services such as car wash and lounge
Battery charging scheduling, peak power management, and electricity cost optimization
Solar integration and station energy flow management
Robot and vision technology to recognize differences between vehicle models, enabling support for various EVs without vehicle modification
Incheon No. 2 Mega Station designed for 200 swaps/day and 500 membership charges/day (planned)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: It operates its own in-house developed battery swapping system, currently in its second generation. It is developing 'Station-to-Grid (S2G)' technology to bi-directionally connect swapping stations with the power grid. A R&D plan of approx. KRW 4B over three years (including KRW 3B in government grants) was announced. Robot and vision-based vehicle type recognition is presented as a key differentiator.
product.target_customer: Drivers and operators of commercial EVs such as taxis and trucks (individual and corporate). It is also known to be developing station installations within large logistics centers for logistics company vehicles.
product.business_model: Battery swap subscription fees and membership charging fees are the primary revenue. It aims to manage the full lifecycle of commercial EVs by adding EV maintenance, parts development, and trade (used vehicle) businesses. Station energy operations and power grid-linked revenue are confirmed to be in the planning stage.

direct_competitors.name: EV Monster
direct_competitors.comparison: A hardware-focused company that makes remotely controlled smart EV chargers. It does not operate battery swapping or subscription models, so it is not a direct competitor to PIT IN, but they are compared together in the commercial EV charging infrastructure market.

direct_competitors.name: Green Dot
direct_competitors.comparison: Classified as an EV charger manufacturer. Its business structure focuses on charger equipment sales, which differs from battery swap services.

direct_competitors.name: Korea Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Technology
direct_competitors.comparison: Operates EV chargers and a dedicated charging station search service. There is overlap in charging infrastructure, but battery swapping and a subscription model for commercial vehicles are not confirmed.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: It combines operational experience in battery swapping specialized for commercial EVs with a S2G plan to connect stations to the power grid. Unlike charger manufacturers, it directly handles battery assets and operational data.
competitive_landscape.moat: The swapping and charging data accumulated from station operations, battery status information, relationship with Hyundai Motor Group, and track record of government R&D and innovation project selections could serve as barriers to entry. However, technology patents or economies of scale are not yet confirmed from public data.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: It appears to be an early leader in the domestic commercial EV battery swapping sector, but market share or competitor scale is not confirmed. Since it is in a different area from charging infrastructure companies, direct comparison metrics are limited.

ad-system-adsystem-inc-2026.tagline: Developer of low-observability VTOL fixed-wing UAVs that withstand anti-drone environments

founders.background: After graduating in aeronautical engineering, he served as an Air Force non-commissioned officer maintaining reconnaissance and training aircraft. He later worked as a development team leader at a civilian drone company and founded AD System in May 2019 based on that experience. He stated his motivation was to create a company that designs airframes directly, rather than assembling Chinese components.
founders.notable_achievement: The company and media announced that its flagship AD-3000 was commercialized as Korea's first stealth VTOL reconnaissance UAV. According to reports, low-observability performance was verified in ADD RCS tests and at Ohio State University's ESL test facility, with the latter being unique among domestic companies.

ad-system-adsystem-inc-2026.team_highlights: In this survey, co-founder information other than CEO Jung-ho Kim was not confirmed. The company said in an interview that initially four developers handled everything from design to test flights themselves. Investment evaluators highly rated the company as one of the few domestic firms that performs airframe design, composite manufacturing, flight control and avionics software, and system integration entirely in-house. The initial investor is JB Ventures, and the company came from IBK Industrial Bank's startup incubation program IBK Changgong.

product.summary: Designs and manufactures small stealth VTOL fixed-wing UAVs. The main model is the reconnaissance AD-3000, with the attack-type AD-4000 targeted for completion by 2027. It also sells educational multirotors.
product.problem_statement: With the widespread deployment of C-UAS systems, UAVs on the battlefield are easily detected and shot down by jamming or interception. The company argues that expensive UAVs usable only in small numbers have limitations.
product.solution: Combines low-observability (radar cross-section reduction) design and stealth paint, VIO/SLAM-based navigation without GPS, anti-jamming datalinks, and terminal-stage evasive maneuvers. It also aims to extend endurance through fixed-wing cruise and lower unit costs for mass supply.
key_features: AD-3000: Fixed-wing design that takes off and lands vertically via propellers and cruises on wings; up to 3 hours flight (company stated)
RCS reduction of over 90% and maximum endurance of 90+ minutes (per media reports)
Development of non-GPS navigation (VIO/SLAM), anti-jamming datalink, and terminal-stage evasive flight technology
AD-4000: Stealth attack-type airframe targeting 15kg payload and 5-hour flight (DSK 2025 data, under development)
Company states auto takeoff and landing enables operation without professional pilots
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Airframes are made from carbon composite molding, integrated with in-house developed flight control and avionics software. The company says low-observability shape design (applying radar-absorbent paint only to high-reflectivity areas and using airframe angles and structure to scatter waves elsewhere) reduces weight and flight efficiency issues.
